info.title: Cachet API
info.description:
Issuance console and verifiable registry for Zcash Shielded Assets (ZSA), running against the public ZSA testnet.

Everything the registry serves is **derived from the chain** and independently checkable: metadata hashes participate in the asset id itself (ZIP 227), so a response can be re-verified client-side. The public instance at `api.cachetzec.com` is **read-only** — every mutating `issuance` endpoint answers 403 there; browser mints go through `POST /api/v1/relay`, which only forwards signed bytes.

Rate limit: 30 requests/s per client, bursts of 60 - sized for a real session, a browser wallet paging through the chain included. Need better limits, or none at all? Run your own instance: the code is MIT, the limit is one environment variable (`CACHET_RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC`, `0` disables it), and the public ZSA node accepts transactions directly. This deployment is a convenience, never a chokepoint.

No cookies, no telemetry, and no authentication anywhere except the optional operator surface.

get.summary: List every asset observed on the chain, newest first.
get.description:
`resolved=true` narrows the listing to assets whose description is
known, which is what a client wants when it intends to show names
rather than ids. Everything stays reachable without it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Keep only the newest N assets. Omitted: the whole registry (what a
client doing its own search or mirroring wants).

parameters.name: resolved
parameters.description:
`true`: keep only assets whose description is known, so their name
is attested rather than an id. Omitted: everything, which stays the
default - this is a caller's view preference, never moderation.

post.summary: Issue units of an asset (creates the asset on first issuance).

Mint several assets in ONE transaction (a single ZIP 227 issuance
bundle, one action per item, all-or-nothing).

get.summary:
Read the on-chain state of an asset, with its registry enrichment
(journaled description, display name, image) when known.

post.summary: Permanently destroy units of an asset held by the wallet.
Teach the registry the plaintext description of an on-chain asset.
post.description:
Verified, permissionless, and deliberately open on read-only
deployments: the chain stores only the description hash (ZIP 227), so a
submission either matches the on-chain commitment or is rejected — the
registry cannot be lied to. This is how assets issued elsewhere gain
names here.

422.description: The description does not hash to the on-chain commitment

get.summary: Identify the connected network and chain tip.
Raw transactions of a block range, for client-side note scanning.
get.description:
Public chain data, identical for every caller — a browser wallet
downloads these pages and trial-decrypts locally, so this instance
never learns which notes belong to whom (PRIVACY.md). Open on
read-only deployments for the same reason as description resolution:
serving public data is not signing.

parameters.name: start_height
parameters.description: First block height of the page (min 1).

get.summary:
Chain-level collections: every asset minted under one issuance key,
grouped — the only provenance statement the chain itself makes.

post.summary:
Register a metadata bundle and get back the on-chain description that
binds it to the asset at issuance.

410.description: These exact bytes were withheld or purged by this registry's operator

429.description: This client's upload budget for the minute is spent, or the pending-upload pool is at capacity

get.summary:
Fetch a metadata bundle by its content hash. Verifiable: re-hash the
body and compare with the path.

200.description: The bundle JSON, byte-exact as stored

get.summary:
Serve the image embedded in a metadata bundle (same-origin, so the
console never fetches third-party assets — PRIVACY.md P5).

post.summary: Relay a fully signed, browser-built issuance transaction to the chain.
post.description:
Deliberately open on read-only deployments: read-only means "this
instance signs nothing", and a relayed transaction was signed by the
sender's own browser-held key. The relay can refuse; it cannot alter.

429.description: This client already has the maximum number of relays in flight; retry shortly

get.summary:
Signed registry snapshot: a deterministic export of every asset the
registry knows, sealed under the operator's Ed25519 key so mirrors can
serve it offline and clients can verify it (see the registry spec for
the verification procedure). 503 until the operator configures
CACHET_SNAPSHOT_KEY.
Spendable balances of the wallet's tracked accounts.
get.description:
Disabled on read-only deployments: the operator's shielded balances are
exactly the kind of information this project exists to keep private,
and a public instance must not broadcast them.

get.summary:
Liveness probe. Does not touch the chain: a wedged node must not make the
process look dead.

AccountBalancesResponse.description: Spendable balances of one wallet account.

AssetEventResponse.description:
One public event of an asset's life. Transfers are shielded and never
listed.

amount.description: Units issued or burned; zero for finalization.

AssetSummaryResponse.description:
The public record of one asset: a registry listing row, and also the
full response of the single-asset endpoint.

description.description:
Raw chain description, when known. The chain only stores the
description hash, so this is present only for assets issued through
this instance (local journal).

display_name.description:
Safest human-readable name derived from the description: the sealed
envelope name or the raw free text. Render it according to
`name_source`.

image_path.description:
Server-relative path to the asset's image (serve from the API
origin), when a stored metadata bundle embeds one.

issuer.description:
The issuance validating key that minted this asset (ZIP 227
canonical encoding, lowercase hex). The chain's only provenance
statement: assets sharing this key share an issuer.

name_source.description:
Where `display_name` comes from — `envelope` (sealed into the asset
id) or `free_text` (issuer-chosen, unverified label). Anti-phishing:
clients must not present a name without its provenance.

BatchIssueRequest.description: Request body for minting several assets in one transaction.

items.description:
1–16 items, no duplicate descriptions. The whole batch lands in one
issuance bundle: one transaction, one txid, all-or-nothing.

BatchIssueResponse.description: Result of an accepted batch issuance.

asset_ids.description: Minted asset ids, in request order.

txid.description: The single transaction that minted every asset in the batch.

BurnAssetRequest.description: Request body for burning units of an asset from the wallet.

amount.description: Units to permanently destroy; must be greater than zero.

ChainInfoResponse.description: Connected network, chain tip, and deployment mode.

read_only.description:
When true, the wallet-signing endpoints (mint, batch mint,
transfer, burn, wallet) answer 403 — a public read-only
deployment. Relay, description resolution and metadata upload stay
open: they need no key from this instance.

snapshot_public_key.description:
Ed25519 public key (hex) that signs this instance's registry
snapshots; absent when snapshots are not enabled. Compare it to
the operator's out-of-band publications (working paper, posts)
before trusting a mirror.

tip_height.description: Chain tip height as seen by the node.

CollectionResponse.description: A chain-level collection: every asset minted under one issuance key.

finalized_count.description: How many of the issuer's assets are finalized.

issuer.description: Issuance validating key, ZIP 227 canonical encoding, lowercase hex.

total_supply.description: Sum of the circulating supplies of the issuer's assets.

HoldingResponse.description: One asset held by a wallet account.

IssueAssetRequest.description: Request body for issuing units of an asset.

amount.description: Units to issue; must be greater than zero.

description.description:
Asset description (1–512 bytes). Immutable once first issued: together
with the issuer key it determines the on-chain asset id.

finalize.description: Permanently disable further issuance after this transaction.

asset_id.description: Id of the minted asset — use it with `GET /api/v1/assets/{asset_id}`.

txid.description: Transaction id (hex, display order). Acceptance, not finality.

MetadataUploadRequest.description: Request body for registering a metadata bundle before issuance.

description.description: Long-form description (≤ 4096 bytes), stored in the bundle only.

image_data_uri.description: Embedded image as a base64 data URI (png/jpeg/webp/gif, ≤ ~400 KB).

name.description:
Display name (1–120 bytes); becomes part of the immutable on-chain
description.

MetadataUploadResponse.description:
Result of a metadata upload: the bundle hash and the exact description
string to use at issuance (which binds the bundle to the asset forever).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored bundle bytes, hex-encoded.

bytes_present.description:
Bundles only: whether this registry still holds the bytes
(`false` after a purge). `null` for other kinds.

key.description: Hex-encoded key: bundle sha256, asset id, or issuance validating key.

purge.description:
Bundles only: also delete the bytes from this registry's store.
The moderation entry stays, so the same bytes are refused if
re-uploaded; the chain commitment and the name are untouched.

reason.description: Optional operator note, stored with the entry (audit trail).

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 problem document. Every non-2xx response uses this shape.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.

status.description: HTTP status code, duplicated for clients that drop it.

RawBlockResponse.description: One block's raw transactions, hex-encoded, consensus order.

txs.description:
Every transaction of the block (coinbase included), raw hex. Order
matters: client-side note scanning must append commitments in
exactly this order.

RawBlocksResponse.description:
A page of raw blocks for client-side note scanning. Public chain data,
identical for every caller: browsers scan for their own notes locally
and never tell the server which notes are theirs.

tip_height.description: Chain tip at the time of the call: fetch until `height == tip_height`.

RelayRequest.description:
Request body for relaying a browser-built, fully signed transaction.

The instance signs nothing: the transaction was built, proven and
signed in the sender's browser (see the mint engine). The relay can
refuse, never alter. Available on read-only deployments — the whole
point is that the server holds no keys.

ResolveDescriptionRequest.description:
Request body for resolving an asset's on-chain description.

Permissionless by design: the chain stores only the description hash
(ZIP 227), so a preimage either matches the commitment or is rejected —
the registry cannot be lied to. This is how assets issued by *other*
parties gain names here.

SnapshotResponse.description:
The wire envelope: payload bytes plus a detached signature. Mirrors
store and serve this JSON as-is.

payload.description: Base64 of the canonical payload JSON (see `SnapshotPayload`).

public_key.description: Hex Ed25519 public key of the signing operator.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the decoded payload bytes.

signature.description: Hex Ed25519 signature over ("cachet-snapshot-v1" || sha256 bytes).

tip_height.description: Convenience mirrors of payload facts (unsigned; trust the payload).

TransferAssetRequest.description: Request body for transferring units of an asset from the wallet.

amount.description: Units to move; must be greater than zero.

recipient.description:
Destination: a unified address with an Orchard receiver, or
`account:N` for one of the wallet's own accounts (demo convenience).

TxResponse.description: A transaction accepted by the chain.

txid.description: Transaction id (hex, display order). Acceptance, not finality.

tags.name: registry
tags.description: The public registry, derived from the chain: assets, issuers, per-asset history, and permissionless description resolution (accepted only when it hashes to the on-chain commitment).

tags.name: metadata
tags.description: Content-addressed metadata bundles. A bundle's SHA-256 travels inside the on-chain asset description, so what these endpoints serve can never be silently swapped.

tags.name: chain
tags.description: Raw chain access: network info, raw blocks for local wallet scanning (identical bytes for every caller), and the relay that forwards signed transactions without seeing a key.

tags.name: issuance
tags.description: Server-wallet issuance for self-hosted deployments. Disabled (403) on public read-only instances — mint from the browser instead.

tags.name: snapshot
tags.description: Deterministic registry export, sealed under the operator's Ed25519 key. Any mirror can serve it; any client can verify it (format in packages/registry-spec).

tags.name: ops
tags.description: Liveness, and the optional token-gated operator surface (absent — 404 — unless CACHET_ADMIN_TOKEN is set).
